title: Sentinel token duplication after quantize swap - incident review
summary: This doc captures the incident on 2025-11-04 where a canary rollout of a newly quantized model variant caused duplicate sentinel tokens to appear in generated structured outputs, breaking downstream JSON parsing for several clients in eu-west-1. We aborted the rollout, rolled back to the previous variant, and validated consumer-facing behavior. Root cause appears to be an interaction between an updated tokenizer merge step and a quantize index truncation bug that produced index collisions for sentinel IDs.
detailed_notes:
Background:
- Deployment: canary rollout of model v3.2-q4b to 10% capacity in eu-west-1 (edge).
- Intended change: switch to the new 4-bit quantized build (q4b) created by the new quantize pipeline (GH-ops/quantize-pipeline). The model was built from model artifacts A and tokenizer artifacts T.

Detection and impact:
- 2025-11-04 03:12 UTC: Alert from prod-synthetics and customer error reports indicating JSON parse failures for structured responses.
- Symptoms: structured responses had duplicated sentinel tokens (e.g., "<|endofanswer|><|endofanswer|>") or the sentinel replaced by a nearby subtoken, causing downstream parsers to either prematurely terminate or treat trailing content as malformed.
- Scope: ~120 requests over 4m window showed duplicates; p95 latency unaffected, but error rate for parseable responses rose to 6% in canary hosts. A small number of paying customers in eu-west-1 experienced mapping failures.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:45: Canary rollout started (10% traffic).
- 03:08: First internal trace with duplicated sentinel logged by canary tracing.
- 03:12: Alerts fired and CS reported customer errors.
- 03:18: On-call SRE (Miguel) began triage; confirmed correlation with canary by comparing canary vs stable traces.
- 03:25: Scoped traffic to 0% for canary as precaution.
- 03:32: Asserted rollback of model routing to stable variant manually by Platform Engineering.
- 03:45: Monitoring showed error rate returned to baseline on stable.
- 05:10: Post-rollback validation and short-term mitigations applied.

Investigation findings:
- Tokenizer artifact T had been regenerated in the quantize pipeline to include an automated "merge optimization" pass intended to reduce vocab size by merging rare subtokens. That pass changed merge ordering for a handful of sequences.
- During quantization, a transient bug in the index mapping step truncated quantized indices for vocabulary entries with IDs >= 65520 when converting from 32-bit to the internal quantized index type used by the runtime. This produced index collisions for a small set of tokens including the sentinel token ID (our internal EOS sentinel).
- The combined effect: new tokenizer mapping assigned a slightly different codepoint to the sentinel, while quantize truncation caused the runtime to resolve two different codepoints to the same internal index — leading to duplicated/split sentinel emission during sampling and greedy decode paths.
- Why only in canary: canary hosts were running the new q4b binary (runtime compiled with the newer quantization index type), whereas stable hosts used the older index handling and older tokenizer. The artifact mismatch (new tokenizer + new runtime) triggered the manifestation in canary traffic only.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled routing back to the stable model variant across eu-west-1 and invalidated canary routing configs.
- Reverted the quantized build availability in the artifact registry to block further deploys.
- Purged edge caches for tokenizer metadata on canary hosts.
- Issued temporary downstream adapter mitigation: for impacted customers we added a tolerant JSON post-processor that allowed single duplicated sentinel deduping as a short-term compatibility shim (feature-flagged).

Root cause (summary):
- Two independent issues combined: (1) a tokenizer merge reordering that changed the assigned codepoint for the sentinel token in the new tokenizer artifact, and (2) an index truncation bug in the quantize pipeline/runtime conversion that created collisions for high IDs. Alone either change would likely not cause visible breakage, but together they produced duplicated sentinel emission.

Contributing factors:
- Lack of a tokenizer+quantize cross-check in the pre-deploy test matrix that validates sentinel identity invariants (unique ID and collision-free mapping).
- Artifacts (tokenizer and quantized weights) were built in separate steps in CI with only a lightweight hash check on each, not an integrated end-to-end decode sanity run.
- Canary sizing small (10%) limited blast radius but still allowed user-visible errors.

Permanent fixes and follow-ups:
- Short term (P0): Add a hotfix to the quantize pipeline to ensure no truncation of vocab indices during format conversions. Ticket: JIRA-SRE-4512 (assigned to Samir).
- Mid term (P1): Extend the pre-deploy CI checks to perform a lightweight decode test that asserts sentinel tokens are unique and round-trip unchanged after quantize+pack steps. GH-ops task: add "tokenizer-sentinel-check" to pipeline and block merges if check fails.
- Mid term (P1): Include an integration test in the artifact registry that pairs tokenizer artifact with quantized weights and runs a small batch of inference cases including structured-output examples.
- Long term (P2): Replace the internal quantized index conversion to use a checked integer type and fail-fast if out-of-range mapping would occur; add telemetry to capture any collisions in decodes.
- Runbook change: Add a dedicated troubleshooting checklist "sentinel-duplication-or-missing" under SRE runbooks with quick checks (hashes, artifact pair sanity, decode sample).

Runbook / checklist (draft):
1) If structured output parse errors spike concurrently with a model rollout: check canary vs stable artifact hashes for tokenizer and weights.
2) Pull a sample of canary-generated outputs; search for sentinel repeated sequences or substitutions.
3) Inspect quantize pipeline logs for "index-map" steps for warnings about truncation.
4) If detected, stop canary routing and revert to stable immediately.
5) Block artifact registry version and inform CS + affected customers.
6) Apply tolerant dedupe transformer only as temporary mitigation and track via feature-flag.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- JIRA-SRE-4512: Fix quantize index truncation bug (Samir) - ETA 2025-11-07.
- GH-ops/quantize-pipeline#679: Add tokenizer-sentinel-check to CI (Miguel) - ETA 2025-11-10.
- SRE-RB-22: Add "sentinel-duplication" troubleshooting section to SRE runbook (Priya) - ETA 2025-11-09.
- Add telemetry metric for duplicate sentinel detection in decode pipeline (Ava) - ETA 2025-11-14.

Customer communications:
- CS draft prepared for impacted customers explaining rollback and short-term mitigation; offered one-week credit for affected tenants. CS ticket: CS-2025-998.

Lessons learned:
- Artifact parity checks must be end-to-end for changes that touch tokenizer or encoding layers.
- Small quantization/serialization bugs can have outsized functional impacts when they collide with sentinel or control tokens.
- Canary deploys need automated decode-sanity gates as early-warning measures (not just perf/latency SLOs).

Appendix - quick diagnostics commands used during triage:
- Verify tokenizer hash on canary host: gsutil cat gs://artifacts/tokenizers/T-v3.2.json | sha256sum
- Compare runtime index table: curl canary-host/_internal/index-map | jq .table | head
- Sample decode dump: curl canary-host/infer -d '{"prompt":"<|s|>...","max_tokens":80}' | jq -r .output | sed -n '1,120p'

Notes to engineering reviewers:
- We have a separate follow-up doc planned to propose an invariant for sentinel tokens across all pipelines (format, ID range, reserved slots). This incident highlights the need to reserve low IDs for special tokens and to fail builds when those invariants are violated.

Status: in_review — please comment inline on suspected remediation design and suggested test vectors to include in CI.

Prepared by: Priya Kapoor (on-call lead for SRE), 2025-11-06
